Fix: in restart(), change those `console.log` calls to `note()`, or have relaunch_detached send the detached copy's stdout into sustain.log.

Because of finding 1, a restart_servex caller can no longer tell a refusal from a success. Its own restart-*.log now holds only the hop line, and the "not restarting" reason goes nowhere. The old description promised "a refusal is written in that log". The fix for finding 1 covers this too, as long as the refusal lines go to sustain.log.

`API` is still hard-coded to 127.0.0.1:8090 (Servex/sustain.mjs:126 before the patch). So in the private proof, the mid-turn check and the "is it back" check were probably talking to the REAL Servex, not the stand-in. The pid-change result (28360→24632) is still convincing, but the proof's "a new one serving /api/agents" was likely the real one answering. Pointing API at SERVEX_HOME, or at a port env var, would make future proofs safe.

The first proof attempt restarted the real Servex (task.jsonl, 16:35 caveat). Pinning SERVEX_HOME fixes that particular leak, but finding 3 is the same kind of leak, so a test harness should pin the port as well.
relaunch_detached builds a `cmd.exe /c set "SERVEX_HOME=..."&& ...` line. A HOME path containing `&`, `%` or `^` would break it. That is unlikely under %LOCALAPPDATA%, but worth a comment.

assign.title: Servex: --restart now hops outside its own process tree
assign.outcome:
**`--restart` can no longer kill the agent doing the restarting.** On win32 it now relaunches itself through WMI (parented to WmiPrvSE, never to Servex), so a tree-kill of Servex can't also kill the caller mid-restart — the exact bug from 09-28/09-29.

- [x] restart via WMI, no window: confirmed live by mastermind-servex-5 — real Servex pid 33112 → 32244, sustain.log shows "relaunched detached... parent WmiPrvSE" then "back as pid 32244"
- [x] ops.js restart_servex goes through the same path — unchanged, already calls `sustain.mjs --restart`
- [x] kill() verifies the pid actually died and retries
- [x] proved on a private stand-in Servex, caller nested inside its own tree
